description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.
intuition: Imagine stacking all the strings on top of each other and reading down each column. The common prefix is the longest column where every string has the same character. Stop as soon as you find a mismatch or reach the end of any string.
approach: Compare characters column by column across all strings. Start with the first character position and check if all strings share the same character at that position. Stop when a mismatch is found or a string ends.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: strs = ["flower","flow","flight"]

i=0: referenceChar="f"
  j=1: strs[1][0]="f" matches
  j=2: strs[2][0]="f" matches
i=1: referenceChar="l"
  j=1: strs[1][1]="l" matches
  j=2: strs[2][1]="l" matches
i=2: referenceChar="o"
  j=1: strs[1][2]="o" matches
  j=2: strs[2][2]="i" != "o" -> mismatch!
  Return strs[0].substring(0,2) = "fl"

Return "fl"
explanation:
1. Use the first string as a reference.
2. For each character position i, check if all other strings have the same character.
3. If any string is too short or has a different character, return the prefix so far.
4. If the loop completes, the entire first string is the common prefix.
hints: Compare character by character across all strings simultaneously.
Stop as soon as you find a mismatch at any position.
The common prefix cannot be longer than the shortest string.

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: N = strings; L = shortest string length.

phases.label: Compare character columns until a mismatch or end
Copy the returned prefix if needed

timeComplexityBreakdown.note: At most L matching columns and one failing column are examined. The +1 also covers checking empty strings. Python’s strs[1:] slice costs O(N) per column and fits this same bound.
